P8f: Then consider practical power. Who actually controls resources? Who has title to property, and control over housing, food stores, vehicles, tools, outside bank accounts, etc.? Who holds the records? Who selects new members? Who selects the reviewers? Who decides access to the kids? To medicine? Who has the ability to stop a complaint from being heard? It may be that the organization chart is horizontal, but that the person who has the keys, passwords, job titles, reputation, etc. is the same person.
P9f: Remember, it's not an override unless it can actually work on the person in question. If the founder selects the person to review the founder, holds the records, has title to the land, and can kick out complainers, then there's no way to override the founder, no matter how many circles the community holds.
